title: M2M-to-FK migration silently drops additional fast associations
reasoning: The original schema permits a Day to be linked to multiple Fast records through the fasts many-to-many field. The forward migration picks only day.fasts.all().first() and stores that single value in _fast. The reverse migration then reconstructs the M2M from only _fast, so any Day with more than one related fast loses all but one association across a forward/reverse cycle or if later migrations remove the M2M field.
recommendation: Before collapsing to a single FK, either enforce that every Day has at most one related fast and fail the migration when violations exist, or model the data in a way that preserves multiple associations. If the business rule is now one fast per day, add an explicit validation/data-cleanup migration that handles conflicts deterministically.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No migration tests or data-shape assertions are included to cover Days with multiple related fasts.
suggestedRegressionTest: Seed a Day with two related Fast records before 0012, run the migration, and assert that the migration either preserves both relationships through the intended new model or fails with a clear error requiring manual cleanup.
minimumFixScope: Change 0012_fast_m2m_to_fk_mapping.py to detect and handle multi-fast Day rows explicitly.
